candidates.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
candidates.content: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrati

candidates.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
candidates.content: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and rea

candidates.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
candidates.content: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. candidates.title: datasette-llm 0.1a11
candidates.content: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a11 datasette-llm is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins. This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol. This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0 ) you can run Datasette via uvx like this: wget https://datasette.io/content.db uvx --with datasette-agent datasette \ --root --secret 1 \ -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model ' { "model": "lmstudio-qwen", "model_name": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b", "api_base": "http://localhost:1234/v1" } ' content.db And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model! candidates.title: FAM50A restrains METTL3–METTL14 catalytic activity to regulate m6A deposition and cell proliferation
candidates.content: Abstract N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is the most abundant internal modification in eukaryotic messenger RNA (mRNA) and is substantially deposited co-transcriptionally by the METTL3–METTL14 methyltransferase complex. However, how chromatin-associated factors modulate the catalytic activity of the m 6 A writer complex remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FAM50A as a chromatin-associated negative regulator of m 6 A deposition. Histone TurboID-based chromatin proteomics and biochemical analyses revealed that FAM50A directly interacts with METTL3. Acute depletion of FAM50A resulted in a global increase in mRNA m 6 A modification, as demonstrated by quantitative, single-nucleotide-resolution GLORI. Mechanistically, FAM50A directly restrains METTL3–METTL14 methyltransferase activity without interfering with RNA substrate binding, thereby limiting excessive m 6 A deposition. Increased m 6 A following FAM50A depletion exerted transcript-dependent effects on mRNA stability, promoting destabilization of a subset of proliferation-associated transcripts while stabilizing others. candidates.title: Excessive PCNA-associated mismatch repair proteins on chromatin by ATAD5 deficiency confers alkylating sensitivity
candidates.content: Abstract Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) acts as a central scaffold coordinating DNA replication and repair. Precise regulation of PCNA loading and unloading is therefore essential for maintaining genome stability. ATAD5, a component of an RFC–like complex, functions as the primary PCNA unloader; however, how defective PCNA clearance influences DNA damage responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we report that loss of ATAD5 selectively enhances cellular sensitivity to alkylating DNA damage through a mismatch repair (MMR)-dependent mechanism. ATAD5 depletion caused persistent retention of PCNA on chromatin, resulting in excessive accumulation of PCNA–associated MMR proteins without altering their overall expression levels. Upon exposure to O 6 –methylguanine-inducing alkylating agents, ATAD5–deficient cells exhibited pronounced increases in chromatin–bound MMR factors, elevated DNA double–strand break (DSB) markers, and enhanced apoptotic responses. Importantly, co–depletion of MSH2 suppressed both DNA damage signaling and cell death, indicating that the cytotoxic effects observed in ATAD5–deficient cells are largely mediated by aberrant MMR activity. candidates.title: A deep-learning predictive model for Cas12a activity in wheat
candidates.content: CRISPR technology has created targeted DNA mutations across the tree of life. Target sites are defined by RNA molecules that largely determine the efficiency of an experiment. Several predictive models are available to select the most efficient RNAs. Unfortunately, these models are not built with plant data and have limited predictive power in plant systems. To overcome this limitation, we established a high-throughput arrayed wheat protoplast transfection method and measured the editing efficiency of ~1,000 unique LbCas12a crRNAs at on- and off-target sites. We trained different models by testing 40 deep learning architectures and found that a convolutional neural network model called 2CaP-5 displayed the best performance. While 2CaP-5 had moderate to strong predictive power in protoplasts, it did not generalize to Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Despite this limitation, we demonstrate that 2CaP-5 can be re-trained with as few as 500 crRNAs. The use of such a small training set is advantageous for low-throughput experimental systems such as typically found in transgenic plant systems. We also used ~2,000 off-targets in the wheat subgenomes to investigate Cas12a specificity.

candidates.content: [NA] COMPLETED | 申办方/赞助方: Saglik Bilimleri Universitesi | 适应症: Human Papillomavirus Infection. This study aims to evaluate the effect of an educational intervention based on the Health Belief Model (HBM) combined with motivational interviewing on women's knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection and their awareness of HPV vaccination. The study will be conducted among women aged 18-45 who have not received the HPV vaccine. Participants in the intervention group will receive structured education and motivational interviews, while the control group will receive no intervention. Changes in HPV knowledge and vaccine awareness will be measured before and after the intervention using validated scales. The goal is to improve preventive behaviors and increase vaccine uptake through behavior-based education.

candidates.title: TETHER: Training-Free, Elastic, ToC-Anchored Hierarchy Extraction and Recovery in Design-Driven Long Documents
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.24960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Converting complex documents into structured knowledge constitutes the critical infrastructure urgently required for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in downstream research. However, blind to the Table of Contents (ToC) as a macro-structure, existing bottom-up paradigms rely on localized visual cues, inducing heuristic fragility in high-entropy layouts where visual prominence decouples from logical depth; meanwhile, direct LLM extraction lacks spatial grounding, triggering hallucinations in long contexts. To address this, we introduce TETHER, a training-free framework that elevates the ToC from discarded noise to a vital structural prior, enabling robust adaptation across design-driven long documents. TETHER operates via a two-stage neuro-symbolic mechanism: first, it constructs a document skeleton from the raw ToC using a Large Multimodal Model (LMM) empowered by spatio-semantic constraints; second, it employs an anchor-based alignment strategy to tether content blocks to this skeleton, effectively resolving boundary ambiguities. candidates.title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.24970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. We instruct LLMs to select questions from this bank in preparing for job interviews, across a set of various occupations and contexts, and report the fraction of unlawful questions that LLMs select. Evaluation of 18 closed and open-weight LLMs across ~100,000 trials under different types of contextual pressure reveals that LLMs' legal compliance is brittle. While LLMs generally avoid selecting unlawful questions in low-pressure contexts, legal violations increase sharply under higher pressure. candidates.title: Stop Going in Circles:Loop-Triggered Routing for System 1 Decision Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.25363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System 1 decision models (represented by Jev) provide fast, low-cost action selection, but existing agent integrations do not reliably translate these local advantages into task completion. At certain points during execution, an agent may repeatedly select the same actions without making progress toward its goal. LLM-based policies offer strong reasoning capabilities that support planning within an agent, but invoking them at every step incurs substantial overhead. The effective coordination should therefore preserve Jev's fast local action selection while introducing LLM reasoning when execution stalls. We observe that recurring state-action pairs can signal stalled execution. We therefore propose LoopRoute, a simple but effective action router that uses this signal to allocate control within an agent. The decision model acts by default. When a loop is detected, the LLM provides brief, feedback-driven assistance and then returns control to the decision model. Later loops can request further assistance. candidates.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. Additional supervision targets tokens admitted by sensitivity or teacher-distribution disagreement, with shared frozen-prior, template-bigram, and student--teacher divergence gates. Inverse-frequency redistribution preserves the total additional weight within each micro-batch, while the positive teacher remains the sole distillation target.
